references.text: The nations heard about Israel's exodus from Egypt and were afraid, just as the kings in Joshua 5:1 feared when they heard about the drying up of the Jordan.
The Lord parted the Red Sea for Israel, a parallel to how He dried up the waters of the Jordan.
Rahab reports that the inhabitants of Jericho had heard about the Lord's mighty deeds and that their hearts melted in fear, the same reaction as the kings in 5:1.
The spies report that the people of the land are gripped with terror over Israel, confirming how widespread the fear has become.
The description of how the Jordan stopped flowing and Israel crossed on dry ground—the very miracle the kings heard about.
The purpose of the drying up of the Jordan was that all the peoples of the earth would know the Lord's power and fear Him, which is fulfilled in 5:1.
Moses' prophecy that fear and dread over Israel would fall upon the nations is fulfilled here.
The Lord promised to put fear and dread of Israel upon all the lands, which happens when the kings hear about the miracle.
